title: Sensitivity labels: what they classify, protect and tell Copilot to leave alone
summary: The service-side auto-labeling control needs a more specific licensing requirement: a client-only P2 entitlement does not establish entitlement to label SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange content. The documented paths and commands otherwise check out, with smaller corrections needed for the Copilot DLP route, conflicting group-update guidance and preview reports.

claims.claim: The classic label-creation route is Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > + Create a label.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels ... On the Sensitivity labels page, select + Create a label

claims.claim: New-Label -Name <label name> -DisplayName <display name> -Tooltip <tooltip> creates a sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Use the New-Label cmdlet to create sensitivity labels in your organization. ... -Name <String> ... -DisplayName <String> ... -Tooltip <String>

claims.claim: Label publishing is under Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > Publish label.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies. ... On the Label policies page, select Publish label

claims.claim: New-LabelPolicy -Name <policy name> -Labels <label names> creates a sensitivity label policy containing the specified labels.
claims.quote: New-LabelPolicy -Name "Research and Development" -Labels "R and D","R and D Management" ... creates the sensitivity label policy named Research and Development that contains sensitivity labels named R and D and R and D Management.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive label support is enabled in Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Turn on now.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels. ... If you see a message to turn on the ability to process content in Office online files, select Turn on now

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true enables sensitivity label support for SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: To enable the new capabilities, use the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet with the EnableAIPIntegration parameter: ... Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document an admin UI for enabling tenant-wide sensitivity label support for Microsoft 365 groups, teams and sites.
claims.quote: Searched: sensitivity labels EnableMIPLabels enable feature admin center UI PowerShell only. Read groups-assign-sensitivity-labels and sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites; enabling uses PowerShell. Their group-label assignment UI is not the tenant enablement control.

claims.claim: Update-MgBetaDirectorySetting -DirectorySettingId <setting id> -BodyParameter <params> enables group labels when the body sets EnableMIPLabels to True.
claims.quote: Name = "EnableMIPLabels" ... Value = "True" ... Update-MgBetaDirectorySetting -DirectorySettingId $grpUnifiedSetting.Id -BodyParameter $params

claims.claim: Service-side auto-labeling policy creation is under Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > + Create auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... Select + Create auto-labeling policy.

claims.claim: New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Name <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -SharePointLocation <SharePointSiteLocation> -ApplySensitivityLabel <Label> -Mode TestWithoutNotifications creates an auto-labeling policy in test mode.
claims.quote: New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Name <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -SharePointLocation "<SharePointSiteLocation>" -ApplySensitivityLabel <Label> -Mode TestWithoutNotifications

claims.claim: The printed Copilot DLP route reaches the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location in the Custom policy wizard.
claims.quote: Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy. ... Select the Custom template, then Custom policy. ... On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.
claims.fix: Extend controls[5].ui.path and the matching rendered cell to 'Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork > rule > Content contains > Sensitivity labels'; keep the note naming 'Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content'.

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <rule name> -Policy <policy name> -AdvancedRule <advanced rule> -RestrictAccess <settings> sets the Copilot content-processing restriction.
claims.quote: New-DLPComplianceRule -Name "Copilot Rule" -Policy "Copilot Policy" -AdvancedRule $advrule -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="ExcludeContentProcessing";value="Block"})

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels are Microsoft Purview Information Protection classifications.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels from Microsoft Purview Information Protection let you classify and protect your organization's data

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels can encrypt files.
claims.quote: apply a "Confidential" label to a document or email, and that label encrypts the content

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels can encrypt emails.
claims.quote: Control access to content by using encryption for emails, meeting invites, and documents

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels can control site privacy settings.
claims.quote: Protect containers ... For example, set privacy settings, external user access and external sharing

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels can control site sharing settings.
claims.quote: These settings include privacy settings, external user access and external sharing

claims.claim: Administrators can use labels to govern who can read protected content.
claims.quote: Control access to content by using encryption ... to prevent unauthorized people from accessing this data. You can also choose which users or groups have permissions

claims.claim: Administrators can use labels as conditions to restrict what Copilot may process.
claims.quote: You can create a DLP policy to prevent these Copilot experiences from using files and emails that have sensitivity labels when generating responses.

claims.claim: Applying a sensitivity label is like stamping content.
claims.quote: When you assign a sensitivity label to content, it's like a stamp that you apply.

claims.claim: Labels are stored in file metadata.

claims.claim: Labels are stored in email metadata.
claims.quote: the label is stored in clear text in the metadata for files and emails

claims.claim: Metadata makes labels persist with content wherever it is saved.
claims.quote: Because the label is stored in metadata for files and emails, the label stays with the content, no matter where you save or store it.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels can enforce content markings.
claims.quote: Mark the content when you use Office apps, by adding watermarks, headers, or footers

claims.claim: Administrators create labels.
claims.quote: admins, end users, and then Office or third-party apps or services that respectively create labels, apply them, and enforce the label settings.

claims.claim: Administrators publish labels in label policies.

claims.claim: Users can apply labels manually.

claims.claim: Office and other supporting apps or services enforce label settings.
claims.quote: Office or third-party apps or services that respectively create labels, apply them, and enforce the label settings.

claims.claim: Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator and Security Administrator role groups are documented alternatives for label-management permissions.
claims.quote: Another option is to add users to the Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator, or Security Administrator role group.

claims.claim: Those label-management permissions are not required just to apply labels.
claims.quote: These permissions are required only to create and configure sensitivity labels and their label policies. They are not required to apply the labels in apps or services.

claims.claim: Assigning a label to an existing group requires at least Groups Administrator when the user is not the group owner.
claims.quote: Assign a label to an existing group in the Microsoft Entra admin center ... Sign in ... as at least a Groups Administrator.

claims.claim: Group ownership is an alternative privilege for assigning a group label.
claims.quote: Has sufficient privileges to assign sensitivity labels. The user must be the group owner or at least a Groups Administrator.

claims.claim: Sensitivity-label activities are documented in Audit log activities.
claims.quote: Audit sensitivity labeling in my organization | Audit log activities - Sensitivity label activities

claims.claim: Information Protection reports are in the Microsoft Purview portal under Information Protection > Reports.
claims.quote: You find Posture Reports in the Microsoft Purview portal: Information Protection > Reports ... Information Protection posture reports ... These reports are in preview.
claims.fix: Replace the reports sentence with 'Information Protection posture reports are in preview and are in the Microsoft Purview portal under Information Protection > Reports.' The source addition is covered by the grouped missing-citations finding.

claims.claim: Label-policy order determines which settings win when policies conflict.
claims.quote: If there's a conflict in settings from multiple policies, the settings from the policy with the highest priority (highest order number) is applied.

claims.quote: select Turn on now ... The command runs immediately and when the page is next refreshed, you no longer see the message or button.
